title: What are the Big Four, and how is their consulting different from MBB?
description: Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG explained: their size, their strategy arms, the kind of consulting work they do and how it compares with MBB.
hook: The Big Four are some of the largest employers of consultants in the world, and for many people they are the best place to start a consulting career. Here is what they are, how their consulting differs from MBB, and how to target the right part of each firm.
body:
Who they are

Deloitte, PwC, EY and KPMG began as accounting and audit firms. Today they offer audit, tax, advisory and consulting in more than 150 countries, and together they earned around $220 billion in fiscal 2025.

What their consulting looks like

Big Four consulting is broad. A large share is technology, operations, risk, people and implementation work, often on longer projects with bigger teams. Each firm also has a dedicated strategy arm whose work is closest to MBB:

  • Monitor Deloitte (Deloitte bought Monitor Group in 2013)
  • Strategy& at PwC (formerly Booz & Company), which recruits separately from the rest of PwC
  • EY-Parthenon, EY's strategy arm, with a harder process than EY Consulting
  • KPMG's strategy group

How it differs from MBB

  • Type of work: MBB leans towards strategy; the Big Four lean towards implementation, technology and operations, with strategy in their specialist arms.
  • Size and breadth: the Big Four are far larger and offer many more specialist roles.
  • Interviews: often include group cases, presentations or assessment centres, as well as individual cases and competency questions.
  • Hiring numbers: they hire many more people, so there are more openings at every level.

Which part should you apply to?

Read job titles carefully. "Consulting" at a Big Four firm can mean strategy, technology, risk or human capital, and each has its own interview. Check whether the role uses a case interview, and prepare for that format.
